figures.note: Axes start at zero; dataset scales differ. Dots are origins, not confidence intervals.
Base terminal charge is zero. Initial acquisition is common and excluded; small ordering costs may be visually thin.
Full 0–1 fill scale. Fill is not cycle service probability; zero-demand series have undefined individual fill.
A day with unmet demand in the hypothetical simulator is not an observed historical stockout.
Classes use pre-existing training-prefix EDA, with separate all-zero and insufficient-history groups. Group sizes are in the machine summary.
Buffer is not a calibrated target service level. Lead changes also change the common last supported ordering date.

Association is descriptive, affected by origin volume, bias and scale. No causal or significance inference from 12 points per dataset.
Closing stock and demand have different meanings despite shared unit scale. Complete base events exist for every series/origin; other origins remain inspectable in Parquet.
Colour ranges are symmetric about zero separately by dataset. Scenarios are one-at-a-time stresses, not a joint uncertainty distribution or new tuning search.

qualification: Hypothetical lost-sales simulation; sales are a potentially censored demand proxy. Full populations: Store Item 500 and M5 30,490 series at each of four original validation origins; 28 days per episode. Origins reset stock. Saved forecasts are fixed at issue, not daily refreshed. These validation windows also informed Phase 4 selection; comparisons are exploratory and validation-reused, with no significance claim. Costs are normalised hypothetical units (NCU), not realised savings.
base_assumptions: Base: L=7 full intervening days; R=1; buffer=3 training-mean days; initial=7 days; h=1 NCU/unit/day, p=10 NCU/unmet unit, k=1 NCU/order. Empty initial pipeline. End-day orders arrive start t+L+1. All policies stop new orders when the remaining L+R forecast dates are unavailable; remaining demand is still scored.
